page: Google Cloud Platform n4a-highcpu-4 is an Arm-based virtual machine configured for compute-oriented tasks within the general purpose family. It provides 4 dedicated vCPUs on the arm64 architecture alongside 8.0 GB of system memory, establishing a 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM allocation of 2.0 GB per core. The configuration lacks hardware accelerators, containing zero GPUs.

Storage and networking are structured around modular cloud infrastructure. The instance includes no local storage, requiring attached network persistent disks for filesystem operations and persistent data retention. It also comes with zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses, necessitating Cloud NAT or reserved external IP routing for public network egress and ingress.

From an efficiency standpoint, the lean memory-to-core profile and arm64 execution model offer cost efficiency for parallelized processing where extensive per-thread memory is unnecessary. Tradeoffs include the 2.0 GB per vCPU memory limit, which precludes heavy in-memory data processing, and reliance on remote storage volumes for I/O operations. Appropriate workloads include continuous integration workers, web servers, CPU-focused data transformation, and distributed application microservices.
description: Google Cloud Platform n4a-highcpu-4 is an arm64 compute-oriented instance offering 4 dedicated vCPUs and 8.0 GB of memory, yielding 2.0 GB of RAM per core. Operating without integrated GPUs or local storage, the virtual machine relies entirely on network-attached storage solutions for disk operations and provisions no complimentary public IPv4 addresses. The 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio provides cost efficiency for multi-threaded processes that prioritize raw CPU density over memory footprint. While constrained against large-scale database operations and memory-heavy analytics by its lean RAM profile and lack of local NVMe media, the instance is structured for distributed processing, build servers, microservices, and general compute workloads.
